# High Level Design: Tracora — Asset Management

| | |
|---|---|
| Version | v0.8 |
| Status | Draft |
| Author | Kishore K |
| Date | 2026-08-31 |
| Derived from | Tracora-PRD-Flow-v0.9 |
| Companion | Tracora-LLD-v0.6 |

*This document describes the shape of the system: what the parts are, how they fit, and what the structural decisions are. It does not describe fields, methods or validations — those are in the LLD. Where this document and the PRD disagree, the PRD wins; it is the statement of intent and this is a proposal for meeting it.*

---

## 1. Purpose and audience

This is for whoever reviews the architecture before build, and whoever has to maintain it in two years. It answers: what is being built, what does it depend on, where does it break, and why is it shaped this way rather than some other way.

The PRD it comes from is v0.9, carrying 92 functional and 5 non-functional requirements. Every module below traces to requirements in that document, and the traceability table in section 11 is the map.

## 2. Context

Tracora is a custom Frappe application. It runs inside an existing Frappe bench, on the same site as the HRMS deployment, using the same database and the same login.

| Outside the system | Relationship |
|---|---|
| Frappe framework | Host. Provides ORM, permissions, sessions, scheduler, email queue, REST |
| HRMS / ERPNext | Optional source of company, branch, department and employee data. Tracora reads from it when present and functions without it |
| Desktop browser | Full Tracora interface, used by the asset team |
| Mobile browser | The PWA — scan, search, view. Installed to the home screen |
| SMTP server | Outbound reminder email, via the Frappe email queue |
| Label printer | Receives a print format from the browser. No direct integration |

Two things are deliberately *not* in this picture: there is no separate database, and there is no external service call at any point in a normal flow. Everything Tracora needs is on the site.

## 3. Architectural principles

These four constrain every decision that follows.

**Optional coupling to HRMS.** HRMS is a data source, not a dependency. No Tracora doctype links to an HRMS doctype as a required field, no Tracora module imports HRMS code at module scope, and no scheduled job fails when HRMS is absent. This is NFR-04 and FR-55, and it is the single most structurally significant requirement in the PRD.

**Own the namespace.** ERPNext ships `Asset`, `Asset Movement`, `Asset Category`, `Company`, `Employee`, `Branch`, `Department` and `Location`. Tracora needs concepts with all of those names. Every Tracora doctype therefore carries the `Tracora ` prefix. This costs verbosity and buys immunity from ERPNext upgrades that change those doctypes underneath us.

**Nothing that matters changes by editing a field.** The holder, the owning company and the asset status all move through endpoints that write a movement record. A field edit produces no history, and an edit with no history is invisible to the only thing this system exists to keep.

**Ownership and custody are independent.** Who owns an asset and who currently holds it are two separate facts, recorded separately, because Aionion both places its own devices with clients and manages devices clients own. Collapsing them into one company field makes every ownership total wrong in one direction or the other (FR-73).

**History is append-only.** The custody chain is the reason this system exists. Movement records are written, never updated and never deleted, by any role including Super Admin. This is enforced in code, not by permission alone, because permission can be edited from the UI and code cannot.

**Nothing is scheduled ahead.** Reminders are computed from current record state each day. There is no queue of future emails, because a queued email cannot be recalled when the payment it was chasing has already been made (FR-64).

## 4. Module decomposition

Seven modules inside one app.

| Module | Owns | Requirements |
|---|---|---|
| Masters | Company, branch, department, location, employee. Identity, deduplication, exit status | FR-01 to FR-11, FR-54, FR-56 |
| Assets | The asset register, status and condition, maintenance | FR-12 to FR-19 |
| Assignment | Assign, unassign, transfer, movement history | FR-50 to FR-53, FR-57, FR-58 |
| Tags | Tag mode, series issue, QR generation, label print formats | FR-41 to FR-49, FR-66, FR-67 |
| Licences | Software licences, seats, renewal cycles, date roll-forward | FR-20 to FR-24, FR-59, FR-60 |
| Reminders | Daily evaluation, closing-event suppression, send log | FR-25 to FR-29, FR-63 to FR-65 |
| Access | Mobile PWA, lookup API, reports, exports | FR-30 to FR-40, FR-61, FR-62 |

![Module dependency](data:image/png;base64,)

Dependencies run one way. Masters knows about nothing. Assets depends on Masters. Assignment depends on Assets and Masters. Licences depends on Assets and Masters. Reminders depends on Licences and Assets but nothing depends on Reminders. Access depends on everything and is depended on by nothing.

This matters for one practical reason: Reminders and Access can be built, changed or switched off without touching the record-keeping core.

## 4a. Process pipeline

An asset's life through the system. Every box writes a movement record — that dashed line is the reason the system exists, and no path avoids it.

![Asset process pipeline](data:image/png;base64,)

Three end states, and they mean different things. **Retired** is end of life. **Released** is a client-owned device leaving your care while still perfectly serviceable. **Lost** is neither, and it keeps the last holder's name attached permanently.

The loop between assign, maintain and unassign is where the system spends almost all of its time. Everything else is an edge.

## 4b. Data flow

Where records come from, what they feed, and where they leave.

![Data flow](data:image/png;base64,)

Two things worth reading off it. The subscriber is the only inbound path from HRMS and it has exactly two outcomes — a write to masters, or a conflict record. There is no third branch where it guesses.

And every outbound surface — reports, phone lookup, reminder email — reads from assets and movement history. None of them reads HRMS. That is what makes the independence claim in section 3 true rather than aspirational: pull HRMS out and the left edge of this diagram disappears, while everything to the right of masters carries on.

## 5. Data architecture

Thirteen doctypes. Field-level detail is in the LLD; this is the shape.

**Masters**

- `Tracora Company` — name, address and type (Internal or External), with an optional link to an HRMS company
- `Tracora Branch` — belongs to a company
- `Tracora Department` — belongs to a company
- `Tracora Location` — a physical place with coordinates
- `Tracora Employee` — anyone who can hold an asset, internal staff or a named person at an external company, with a source marker and exit status

**Assets**

- `Tracora Asset` — the register. One row per physical item
- `Tracora Asset Movement` — append-only. Every assignment, unassignment, relocation, status change and label reprint
- `Tracora Maintenance Log` — one row per repair episode, open then closed

**Licences**

- `Tracora Software Licence` — the licence and its dates
- `Tracora Licence Seat` — child table. One row per user-and-device pair

**Operations**

- `Tracora Reminder Log` — append-only. One row per email attempted
- `Tracora Sync Conflict` — an HRMS change that could not be applied, waiting on a person
- `Tracora Settings` — single. Lead days, tag prefix, label dimensions, sender

**Relationship shape**

| Parent | Holds many | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Tracora Company | Branches, Departments, Assets, Licences | Top of the tree |
| Tracora Branch | Employees | Belongs to one company |
| Tracora Department | Employees | Belongs to one company |
| Tracora Employee | Asset assignments, Licence seats | Belongs to one company; branch and department only when internal |
| Tracora Location | Assets currently there | Standalone; not owned by a company |
| Tracora Asset | Movements, Maintenance logs, Licence seats | Points to an owning company, a holding company, a branch and a location; at most one holder |
| Tracora Software Licence | Licence seats | Each seat points to one employee and one asset |

An asset has at most one current holder and exactly one current location. Everything historical lives in movements, not in the asset row. The asset row answers "where is it now"; the movement table answers "where has it been".

**Why a licence seat sits between licence and asset.** A seat names a user *and* a device (FR-21). Modelling it as a child table of the licence rather than a field on the asset means one licence can span many devices, one device can carry many licences, and the exit check has a single place to look. A field on the asset would cap it at one licence per machine.

## 6. HRMS integration

This is where the optional-coupling principle becomes concrete.

**Capability detection, not configuration.** At runtime the integration layer asks the database whether the HRMS doctypes exist. It does not read a settings flag that can be wrong, and it does not import HRMS modules at the top of a file, because a top-level import of an absent module breaks the whole app at load.

**Direction is one way.** Tracora reads from HRMS. It never writes to it. An employee corrected in Tracora does not push back into HR's record, because HR owns that data and a two-way sync between two systems of record produces conflicts nobody has agreed how to resolve.

**Records are copied, not linked.** A `Tracora Employee` sourced from HRMS holds its own copy of the fields, plus a link back to the HRMS record. This is a deliberate reversal of the earlier design, which reused the HRMS employee directly. The reason is FR-55: a link to a doctype that may not exist cannot be a required field, and a system whose employee list vanishes when an app is uninstalled is not independent. The cost is staleness, handled by a re-sync, and duplication, handled below.

**Renames are followed, not re-created.** Frappe allows a document to be renamed, and an employee code is Tracora's primary key. A rename subscriber matches the Tracora record by its stored HRMS reference rather than by code, and renames the Tracora document to match. Without this, every rename in HRMS silently produces a second employee holding no assets, and the original keeps them.

**Deletion in HRMS does not delete in Tracora.** When an HRMS record disappears, Tracora keeps its copy, clears the reference and flips it to Tracora-owned so it becomes editable again. A delete must never cascade into custody history — that history is the reason the system exists.

**Field ownership is explicit.** Every employee field is marked HRMS-owned or Tracora-owned. Read-only applies to the first group only. Aadhaar number and permanent address are always Tracora-owned, whatever the record's source, because HRMS may not hold them and a field that is read-only and permanently empty is a dead field (FR-81).

**A code conflict is an error, not a merge.** Employee code is unique across the whole system regardless of origin (FR-56). When a sync encounters a code that already exists in Tracora, it changes nothing, records the conflict, and reports it. It does not overwrite the Tracora record with HRMS values and does not keep the Tracora values while discarding the HRMS ones. Either automatic rule silently rewrites data a person entered deliberately.

**Propagation is event-driven, because both apps share one site.** Tracora subscribes to HRMS's own document events. When HR saves an employee, Tracora is called in the same transaction and updates its copy immediately. There is no polling, no schedule, and no manual sync button — those exist to bridge two databases, and there is only one here.

A subscription to a doctype that does not exist never fires, so the independence requirement survives untouched. Nothing needs disabling when HRMS is absent.

**One manual action remains, and it runs once.** Employees already in HRMS at go-live were never announced by an event, so a bulk import is needed to seed them. That is a migration step, not an operating feature.

The import runs in dry-run mode first, producing the full conflict list as a report without writing anything. You resolve, then run for real. Installing HRMS onto a Tracora that has been in use for months would otherwise generate a wall of conflict records in one pass, at the worst possible moment for anybody to read them.

**Conflicts are recorded generically.** A conflict names a reference doctype and a key, not an employee code, so a company, branch or department collision has somewhere to go. All of them land on one work list.

**Tracora never blocks an action inside HRMS.** A subscriber that raises an error aborts the caller's save. If Tracora threw on an exit with outstanding assets, HR could not offboard anyone until the asset team collected a laptop — HRMS would be dependent on Tracora, which inverts the entire design. Subscribers record, flag and surface; they never veto. The outstanding-asset block applies to Tracora's own exit action only.

**This mirrors how Frappe's own standalone apps handle a neighbouring app's data.** Frappe CRM owns its doctypes, prefixes them, and treats ERPNext as an integration that is checked for and switched on, rather than a dependency it links into. Tracora takes the same position toward HRMS — with the difference that CRM must support separate sites and therefore syncs, while Tracora is same-site by design and can listen instead.

**The failure this design accepts.** Two people can be entered as two employees under two different codes. Tracora cannot detect that, because it has no other identity to match on. Aadhaar would work as a second key, but matching on it means indexing and querying it routinely, which is exactly the handling the PRD restricts. The system is protected against accidental duplication by code, not against a genuine data-entry mistake by a person.

## 6a. Internal and external companies

Tracora holds two kinds of company and the difference is structural, not cosmetic.

| | Internal | External |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | Part of the group | A client or partner |
| Source | HRMS or Tracora | Tracora only |
| Subscribers | Receives HRMS events | Never touched by HRMS |
| Branch and department | Required | Optional |
| People | `Tracora Employee` | `Tracora Employee` |
| Personal data held | Full employee record | Name, designation, mobile, email. DOB, Aadhaar and address refused |
| Exit process | HRMS-driven, with clearance | Set by hand in Tracora |
| Employee code | From HRMS or typed | Issued from a reserved series |

**One record type holds them all.** A client's engineer and a member of staff are both `Tracora Employee`. An asset, a movement and a licence seat each point at a single employee link — no type field, no dynamic link, no query that has to decide which kind of holder it wants.

**The protection is a validation, not an absent field, and that is weaker.** Date of birth, Aadhaar number and permanent address are hidden and refused on an external-company employee (FR-75). A separate record type would have made those fields not exist, which no configuration change could undo. A validation can be edited by anyone with System Manager, and a hidden field is one property away from visible. This was a deliberate trade of protection for simplicity, and it is recorded here so nobody later assumes the stronger guarantee.

**Reporting still has to distinguish them.** Employee-wise figures mean internal staff; assets with external companies belong in their own report (FR-77). The distinction moved from the record type to the employee's company type — it did not go away.

**Ownership and custody in practice.**

| Situation | Owning company | Holding company | Holder |
|---|---|---|---|
| Staff laptop | Internal | Same internal | Internal employee |
| Device in store | Internal | Same internal | None |
| Device placed with a client | Internal | External | External employee |
| Client's device we manage | External | External | External employee |
| Client's device in for repair | External | Internal | None, status Under Maintenance |

The fourth row is the one that breaks a single-field design: the asset is in the register, it is being tracked and maintained, and it is not yours.

## 7. Reminder architecture

One scheduled job, running daily.

For each open date on each licence and each open maintenance record, the job computes the difference between today and the due date. If that difference is one of the configured lead values — 30, 15, 7, 2, 1 or 0 days — and no log entry exists for that combination, an email is queued and the attempt is logged.

Three properties follow from computing rather than scheduling:

- **Suppression is free.** When a payment is recorded, the payment date rolls forward under FR-23. Tomorrow the job evaluates the new date and finds no match near the old one. Nothing needed cancelling, because nothing had been scheduled (FR-63, FR-64).
- **Restart is free.** The rolled-forward date is a new date. If it falls 20 days out, the 15, 7, 2 and 1 day reminders fire against it in turn (FR-65).
- **A missed run is recoverable, once.** If the scheduler is down on a lead day, that day's email is lost — the job is idempotent, not catch-up. This is a stated limitation, not an oversight: sending a stale "7 days remaining" notice three days late is worse than not sending it.

Delivery is handed to the Frappe email queue. One bad address fails one row in the log and does not stop the run (NFR-05).

## 8. Mobile PWA

The mobile surface is a Frappe portal page, not a separate application. Same site, same session, same permission checks.

| Concern | Approach |
|---|---|
| Install | Web app manifest plus a service worker, installable from the browser (FR-30) |
| Scanning | Camera decoding in the browser. No native app, no app store, no third-party scanner |
| Lookup | One whitelisted server method taking a single string and matching it against tag, serial and asset name (FR-31) |
| Offline | Not supported. The shell may cache; asset data is always fetched live |
| Permission | Server-side on every call. The client is a view, never an authority |

**Why not offline.** An offline cache of asset custody is a copy of who holds what, sitting on a phone, going stale. It would answer questions wrongly with confidence. A search that fails honestly on a bad connection is better than one that answers from last Tuesday.

**Why one lookup method rather than the generic REST API.** A single narrow endpoint returns exactly the fields the screen shows and nothing else. The generic API would let a crafted request pull fields the PWA has no business reading — including the two the PRD restricts.

## 9. Security architecture

**Roles.** Two: `Tracora Super Admin` and `Tracora Admin`. Both read everything; neither is restricted by company or branch. The only difference is delete (FR-19).

**Where enforcement lives.** Role permissions on the doctype for read, write and create. Delete on Super Admin only. Append-only behaviour on movements and reminder logs enforced in code, because a permission can be edited through the UI by anyone with System Manager and code cannot.

**System Manager is the real superuser, not Super Admin.** Anyone holding the stock System Manager role can edit permissions, write script reports and read anything. Tracora cannot constrain that and should not pretend to. The practical control is that System Manager is granted to nobody outside the platform team.

**Restricted personal data.** Aadhaar number and permanent address are readable on screen by both roles and excluded from reports and exports (FR-39). The mechanism is in the LLD. The honest limit: this stops the ordinary export routes — report builder, list export, the standard reports — and does not stop someone with System Manager writing SQL. That is the same person who could grant themselves anything, so the boundary is consistent, but it should be stated rather than implied.

**Audit.** Every doctype tracks changes with user and timestamp (NFR-02). Movement and reminder history is never purged (NFR-03).

## 10. Deployment

Nothing new to run. Tracora installs into the existing bench, on the existing site.

| Concern | Position |
|---|---|
| Install | `bench get-app` then `bench --site <site> install-app tracora` |
| Database | Existing site database. Tracora tables are additive |
| Scheduler | Existing. Tracora registers one daily job. If the scheduler is disabled, no reminders go out and nothing else is affected |
| Workers | Existing. Reminder sends go to the default queue |
| Backup | Existing site backup covers Tracora |
| Environments | Staging install and verification before production |
| Rollback | Uninstall removes Tracora doctypes and their data. There is no partial rollback — a schema change that has run cannot be reversed by uninstalling one app |

**Migration.** Existing asset records, wherever they are held now, need importing. Two things must be decided before that import runs, because both are irreversible in practice: whether existing physical labels are kept as manual-mode tags or the estate is relabelled, and what date is used as the start of history for assets that have been in service for years. Neither is a build question; both block the first import.

## 12. Risks

| Risk | Effect | Position |
|---|---|---|
| Duplicate employees under different codes | Exit check passes while assets remain outstanding on the other record | Accepted. Code uniqueness catches the accidental case; nothing catches a genuine re-entry (§6) |
| Sync conflicts accumulate unread | An employee's Tracora record stays wrong after HR corrects it | Conflicts are recorded as records, not log lines, so they appear as a work list rather than disappearing into a file |
| A subscriber raises an unhandled error | HR's save fails because of Tracora | Subscribers catch their own exceptions and record the failure. A Tracora fault must never surface inside an HRMS action |
| Frappe version unknown | This design assumes v15. Virtual fields, naming and `report_hide` differ on v14 | **Unresolved.** Confirm before build |
| `hrms_custom` may override the HRMS doctypes | Subscribers key on `Employee`, `Company`, `Branch`, `Department`. If any is renamed or wrapped, nothing fires — indistinguishable from HRMS being absent | **Unresolved.** Confirm before build. This is the failure most likely to go unnoticed for weeks |
| `report_hide` may not cover every export route | Aadhaar leaves the system through a path nobody tested | **Unverified.** Must be tested on the target Frappe version before FR-39 is claimed as met |
| Scheduler disabled or failing silently | Reminders stop and nobody notices, because the absence of an email is invisible | Needs a monitoring answer. Not solved by this design |
| System Manager bypasses the PII restriction | Aadhaar and address reachable via custom report or SQL | Accepted and stated (§9). Controlled by who holds the role, not by the app |
| ERPNext upgrade changes an HRMS doctype | Sync breaks | Contained by the prefix and the read-only direction. A broken sync leaves Tracora working on its own records |
| Estate relabelling at migration | Weeks of physical work, or years of mixed tag schemes | Decision needed before first import (§10) |
| Personal-field validation removed or relaxed later | Aadhaar and home addresses accumulate for people who do not work here, with no lawful basis | **Real, and the cost of collapsing the two record types.** The check must be treated as a rule, not a nicety |
| A report forgets to filter on company type | External-company employees are counted as headcount | Real. Every employee-wise figure must filter on internal companies |
| Adoption — movements recorded late or not at all | The register drifts from reality and stops being trusted | Outside the software. No architecture fixes an unused system |
